newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts end higher, outperform, eye rate meeting.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts end higher, outperform, eye rate meeting.

text.p: 1622 GMT - UK gilt futures locked healthy gain on Tuesday, outperforming Bunds and U.S. bonds. But traders said gilts making up lost ground rather than starting new trend. Monetary meeting on Wednesday could spur rally at short end if rates left unchanged. March gilt future settled at 110-05, up 18/32
The monthly monetary meeting between Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Governor of the Bank of England Eddie George is the key focus for sterling markets. It is due to start mid-morning.
A Reuter poll found that none of the 21 economists asked expected rates to move from 6.0 percent.
"There is scope for December short sterling to rally a bit when we get confirmation of no move. It could get up to around 93.75," said Peter Osler, UK economist at GNI.
December short sterling settled at 93.62, down 0.01.
The trader said March short sterling could edge up too.
"March and beyond is still looking too pessimistic. If they don't move (rates) tomorrow the market could start to reassess its interest rate outlook," he said.

U.S. producer prices data will capture the UK market's attention in the afternoon session. PPI is forecast to rise 0.3 percent on the month for a year on year increase of 2.9 percent, slightly lower than October's 3.0 percent. The data are due at 1330 GMT.
"And gilts are going to be a bit jittery ahead of (UK) RPI data on Thursday, although any rate rise on Wednesday would indicate a poor (high) figure," said the trader.
The Reuter poll forecasts retail prices excluding mortgage interest payments rose 3.3 percent in the year to November, unchanged from October. The data are due on Thursday at 0930 GMT.
The long end of the market outperformed on Tuesday.
The benchmark 7.5 percent gilt due 2006 ended the session at 100-01, up 15/32. The benchmark five-year gilt ended at 99-10, up 7/32.
